sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Remove unnecessary adverbs and adjectives from UI copy; they often function as fillers without adding clarity.
claims.quote: Adverbs are words that describe actions like "easily" and "quickly". And adjectives describe nouns. Those include words like "fast" and "simple". Of course, there are many more, and when you notice words like these, it's worth a pause to see if they're needed.

claims.rule: Remove interjections and pleasantries like "oops," "sorry," and "thank you" from error messages and alerts unless they add meaning.
claims.quote: Interjections are abrupt words or phrases like "oops," "oh no," and "hooray." These are remarks used in polite conversation like "sorry," "thank you," and "please." While it might seem like these words make your app feel more personal, it's best to remove them when they don't add any meaning to the message.

claims.rule: Avoid phrases like "uh oh" and "oh no" in error messages; they undermine the seriousness of the problem.
claims.quote: Words like "uh oh, "oops" or "oh no!" in error messages can make it sound like you're not taking the problem seriously.

claims.rule: Lead with the benefit or purpose of an action to give sentences more impact and clarity.
claims.quote: Later, Jen will show you how to lead with the why by doing some hands-on editing to give your sentences more impact.

claims.rule: Create and maintain a word list to ensure consistency across your app's writing.
claims.quote: And she'll conclude by talking about how a word list makes it easy to keep consistency in your app.

claims.rule: Place the benefit or reason first in instructional copy, then the required action, to maximize message impact and clarity.
claims.quote: Effective messaging in apps, such as error messages, push notifications, and instructional copy, is most effective when you clearly state the benefit first, followed by the action required.

claims.rule: Maintain a word list documenting approved terms, avoided synonyms, and definitions to ensure consistent language across the app.
claims.quote: A word list serves as a reference, ensuring use of the same terms throughout an app. This improves people's understanding of the app. Your word list should include approved words, along with synonyms or alternatives to avoid. Add definitions for clarity.

sources.title: Design foundations from idea to interface
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Avoid menus as primary navigation; provide context and clear structure first.
claims.quote: Menus can be vague and unpredictable, and what I really need first is some context.

claims.rule: Organize information by removing non-essential features, clarifying naming, and grouping related items.
claims.quote: I start cleaning things up — removing features that aren't essential, renaming things that aren't clear, and grouping those that naturally belong together.

claims.rule: Use tab bar navigation to help people access main features; limit tabs to essential items only.
claims.quote: Simplifying it matters because each extra tab means one more decision for people to make and might present the app as much more complex that what it really is.

claims.rule: Show only essential upfront; reveal additional content when people interact, not before.
claims.quote: progressive disclosure. It's about showing only what's necessary upfront — just enough to help people get started then revealing more as they interact

claims.rule: Use lists over grids for structured information; lists take less vertical space and scan faster.
claims.quote: A List works way better, it's a flexible, highly usable and familiar way to show structured information and facilitates quick scanning. It also takes up less vertical space than images

claims.rule: Add gradient or blur behind text on images to improve readability without disrupting design.
claims.quote: One simple way to fix this is by adding a subtle background behind the text like a gradient or blur. It improves readability, while adding some dimension

sources.title: Design hover interactions for visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use rounded shapes for interactive elements; they draw eyes to the center and feel more inviting.
claims.quote: For interactive elements, prefer rounded shapes, like circles, pills, and rounded rectangles, they're easier to look at, drawing your eyes to the center of the shape.

claims.rule: Give interactive elements at least 60 points of touch or eye-tracking target space.
claims.quote: For precise interactions, give each element at least 60 points of space. Elements can be visually smaller than this, as long they each have a total space of 60 points.

claims.rule: Apply highlight effects to all interactive elements to signal they are selectable.
claims.quote: Apply highlight effects to all interactive elements. Standard components like this menu will highlight automatically.

claims.rule: Use ramp animations (slow ease-in then quick spring) when views expand to show more content.
claims.quote: To create your own ramp animation, try a curve like this. It starts with a slow ease-in, then pops to completion with a quick spring. This animation curve tends to work best when views expand to show more content.

claims.rule: Use ramp animations (slow ease-in then spring) when views expand to show more content.
claims.quote: It starts with a slow ease-in, then pops to completion with a quick spring. This animation curve tends to work best when views expand to show more content

claims.rule: Show hover effects only from visible elements; hidden content surprises users if revealed accidentally.
claims.quote: hover effects should always start from a visible element. If there's no hint about where something is, it'll be hard to find or surprising if people accidentally discover it

claims.rule: Make scroll views full-width or full-height with clear boundaries so people know where to look to scroll.
claims.quote: your scroll views with Look to Scroll enabled should be the full width or full height of your window. This gives people generous space to scroll and provides clear edges to look at

sources.title: Elevate the design of your iPad app
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Make navigation adaptive; resize without destroying layout, reverting when possible.
claims.quote: When adapting to size changes, make sure that any change in layout is non-destructive. Resizing an app should not permanently alter its layout. Be opportunistic about reverting back to the starting state whenever possible.

claims.rule: Extend content around navigation controls using scroll edge effect and content below sidebars.
claims.quote: People come to your app for its content. So use as much of the display as possible to create the most immersive experience. You can start doing this by drawing content below the toolbar using the new 'scroll edge effect'.

claims.rule: Create new windows for each document in multitasking apps; do not replace previous context in one window.
claims.quote: When multitasking is enabled, your app should open each document in their own window. This additive behavior is more helpful because windows persist until closed

claims.rule: Provide descriptive, unique names for each open window so users can locate them in the app menu.
claims.quote: Name each window with a unique string, like the title of the document. If your app provides a descriptive name for each window, it will be much easier to find a specific window

sources.title: Explore video experiences for visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Spatial video renders with windowed treatment by default; expand immersively to scale content to real size.
claims.quote: By default, spatial video renders through a window, with a faint glow around the edges. It can also expand into an immersive presentation, where the content is scaled to match the real size of objects.

claims.rule: Reduce immersion automatically during high-motion video playback to prevent viewer discomfort.
claims.quote: Playback will automatically reduce immersion when high motion is detected, which can be more comfortable for the viewer during high motion scenes.

claims.rule: Blur window edges for spatial video to prevent stereo discomfort from unequal object clipping between eyes.
claims.quote: We inset that flat screen behind a window and blur the edges of the window to soften them. This helps avoid issues when an object is clipped by the window more in one eye than the other, which can be uncomfortable to view.

sources.title: Optimize your custom environments for visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use billboards for objects beyond 1 kilometer distance where depth perception flattens naturally.
claims.quote: Depth cues start to flatten out from 1 to 3 kilometers. So you can reduce these areas to a flat image without much perceivable loss of depth.

sources.title: Design interactive snippets
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use larger text in snippets to draw attention to important information; text is larger than system defaults.
claims.quote: A key aspect to making the snippet glanceable is type size. Text in snippets are larger than system defaults. Larger type draws attention to the most important information in the moment.

claims.rule: Keep snippet height under 340 points to avoid scrolling; link to app for additional information.
claims.quote: Avoid including content past 340 points in height, which will require scrolling and introduce unexpected friction. Instead, keep the content concise with only the most important information.

claims.rule: Use vibrant backgrounds but check contrast beyond standard ratios; increase contrast for distant viewing.
claims.quote: It's especially important to check for contrast when the snippet is viewed from a distance, going beyond standard contrast ratios. If the content is hard to read, try increasing the contrast between the content in the layout and the background.

claims.rule: Update data within snippet after button action to confirm success and build trust.
claims.quote: By updating the data within the snippet itself to confirm that the action was successful, people can build trust in your App Intent for their routines.

claims.rule: Keep snippet height under 340 points to avoid scrolling and maintain glanceability.
claims.quote: Avoid including content past 340 points in height, which will require scrolling and introduce unexpected friction.

claims.rule: Design snippets to be understood visually without relying on spoken dialog for accessibility.
claims.quote: Challenge yourself to make your snippet understandable on its own, even if the dialog isn't shown or heard. The snippet should clearly communicate the purpose of the intent without relying on dialog.

sources.title: Design widgets for visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use consistent, real-world scale for widgets to feel well-proportioned in any placement.
claims.quote: Widgets have a consistent, real-world scale, helping them to feel well-proportioned wherever they are placed.

claims.rule: Adapt widget appearance and layout based on viewing distance to show appropriate detail levels.
claims.quote: Widgets on visionOS adapt their appearance and layout based on how close someone is, always showing the right level of detail

claims.rule: Design widgets for glanceable legibility from across the room when wall-mounted.
claims.quote: The text size is designed to be glanceable from across the room, ensuring legibility when wall-mounted.

claims.rule: Place widgets on horizontal surfaces at a gentle angle toward the viewer for legibility and grounded appearance.
claims.quote: When placed on a horizontal surface, like a desk, table, or shelf, the widget gently tilts towards the person placing it. This subtle angle helps legibility.

claims.rule: Offer small widget templates for productivity content that fits next to other workspace elements.
claims.quote: If you are designing a productivity-focused widget, you might want to offer it in a small template size so it fits easily on a desk.

claims.rule: Use extra-large widget templates for visually rich, decorative content that functions as statement pieces.
claims.quote: if your goal is to let people decorate their space while using Vision Pro with something visually rich, like an artwork or photography, consider using the extra large template size.

claims.rule: Allow widget resizing from 75% to 125% of base template size while preserving layout integrity.
claims.quote: Each template size can be resized using the corner affordance, scaling from 75% to 125% while still preserving your layout.

claims.rule: Adapt widget information density based on viewing distance using two proximity thresholds.
claims.quote: visionOS provides two key thresholds you can design for. Default, when the widget is viewed up close, and Simplified, when it's seen from a distance.

claims.rule: Scale interactive element targets appropriately for both close and distant viewing in proximity-aware widgets.
claims.quote: Use proximity awareness to your advantage so that the interactive areas of your widget are always easy to target, whether someone is standing close or further away.

sources.title: Meet Liquid Glass
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use lensing to provide visual separation and communicate layering while letting content show through.
claims.quote: Liquid Glass uses these instinctive visual cues to provide separation and communicate layering in a new way while letting content shine through underneath it.

claims.rule: Transition elements by gradually modulating light bending instead of fading for optical integrity.
claims.quote: Instead of fading, Liquid Glass objects materialize in and out by gradually modulating the light bending and lensing, ensuring a graceful transition

claims.rule: Use gradual light modulation instead of fading for material transitions to preserve optical integrity.
claims.quote: Instead of fading, Liquid Glass objects materialize in and out by gradually modulating the light bending and lensing, ensuring a graceful transition that preserves the optical integrity of the material.

claims.rule: Restrict Liquid Glass to navigation layers floating above content; avoid applying it to content tables.
claims.quote: it is best reserved for the navigation layer that floats above the content of your app. Consider this tableview: making it Liquid Glass would make it compete with other elements and muddy the hierarchy.

claims.rule: Never stack Liquid Glass elements; use fills and transparency for overlays instead.
claims.quote: always avoid glass on glass Stacking Liquid Glass elements on top of each other can quickly make the interface feel cluttered and confusing.

claims.rule: Apply tinting selectively to primary actions and elements; avoid tinting all UI components.
claims.quote: Avoid tinting all your elements. When every element is tinted, nothing stands out, and it can be confusing.

claims.rule: Avoid intersections between scrolling content and Liquid Glass; reposition or scale content to maintain separation.
claims.quote: In steady states, such as when an app first launches, avoid intersections between content and Liquid Glass. Instead, reposition or scale the content to maintain separation.

sources.title: Meet SwiftUI spatial layout
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Calculate depth and Z position for 3D views alongside width, height, and XY position in layout systems.
claims.quote: for each of your views, in addition to width and height, SwiftUI also calculates a depth and a Z position.

claims.rule: Use scaledToFit3D modifier to maintain model aspect ratio while scaling across all three dimensions.
claims.quote: scaledToFit3D modifier in addition to resizable(), causing my robot to maintain the model's aspect ratio while still sizing up or down to fit the available width, height, and now depth.

claims.rule: Use scaledToFit3D modifier to maintain model aspect ratio while scaling across all three dimensions.
claims.quote: I can use the new scaledToFit3D modifier in addition to resizable(), causing my robot to maintain the model's aspect ratio while still sizing up or down to fit the available width, height, and now depth.

claims.rule: Customize depth alignment (front, center, back) on Layout types to position 3D views properly.
claims.quote: Just like you can configure in HStack to align its content on the center, top, or bottom edge, you may want to configure how views are aligned in depth on visionOS.

claims.rule: Use SpatialContainer to align multiple views in the same 3D space with 3D alignment guides.
claims.quote: The new SpatialContainer API allows you to place multiple views in the same 3D space like a series of Nesting Dolls. You can apply a three dimensional alignment to all of the views.

claims.rule: Use spatialOverlay to overlay a single view in the same 3D space as another with 3D alignment.
claims.quote: spatialOverlay is a similar tool, which allows you to overlay a single view in the same 3D space as another. Similar to SpatialContainer, it supports 3D alignments.

sources.title: Build a UIKit app with the new design
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Allow tab bars to minimize on scroll to keep focus on content rather than chrome.
claims.quote: With the new design, the tab bar on iPhone floats above the content, and can be configured to minimize on scroll, keeping the focus on your content.

claims.rule: Adjust accessory view visibility when inline with tab bar due to reduced space availability.
claims.quote: When the accessory is inline with the tab bar, there is less space available to display it. Here, the Music app is accommodating the reduced space by hiding some of the media controls

claims.rule: Remove background customization from navigation and toolbars to preserve automatic glass appearance.
claims.quote: Remove any background customization from your navigation and toolbars. Using UIBarAppearance or backgroundColor interferes with the glass appearance.

claims.rule: Limit Liquid Glass to the most important, interactive elements that users touch directly.
claims.quote: Limit Liquid Glass to the most important elements of your app. Where possible, use the system views and controls for the best experience.

claims.rule: Prevent glass elements from overlapping other glass elements to maintain the illusion of a single floating control layer.
claims.quote: This prevents glass elements from overlapping other glass elements, and keeps the illusion of a single floating layer of glass intact.

claims.rule: Use containerRelative corner configuration so glass corners automatically adapt to their container's corners.
claims.quote: To have corners automatically adapt to their container, use .containerRelative cornerConfiguration. When moving the view closer to the container's corner, its corner radius adapts automatically.

claims.rule: Larger glass sizes render more opaque; smaller sizes render clearer and adapt to light or dark mode automatically.
claims.quote: Glass adapts the appearance based on its size. A larger size is more opaque. A smaller size is clearer, and switches between light and dark mode automatically, to increase contrast.

claims.rule: Set isInteractive to true on glass effects for custom views that need button-like scaling and bouncing feedback.
claims.quote: To get that same kind of interactivity in your custom views, set isInteractive to true on the glassEffect.

sources.title: What’s new in SF Symbols 7
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Design symbol paths with draw direction intention: left-to-right for motion, right-to-left for Arabic, center for symmetry.
claims.quote: We've designed Draw to be flexible, allowing each symbol to define how it is drawn. For example, wind draws left to right to convey motion, whereas this Arabic character draws from right to left

claims.rule: Use Variable Draw to render path progress as a percentage with reduced opacity background layer.
claims.quote: Variable draw leverages the new draw annotations on participating layers. It renders the path at a specific percentage on top of a reduced opacity version of the layer.

claims.rule: Place a minimum of two guide points—one start and one end—along each draw path to enable Draw animations.
claims.quote: At a minimum, a path must contain two guide points to properly compute its draw path. A start point, indicated by an open circle, and an end point, indicated by a closed circle.

claims.rule: Design symbol draw directions intentionally: left-to-right for motion, right-to-left for Arabic, center for symmetry.
claims.quote: For example, wind draws left to right to convey motion, whereas this Arabic character draws from right to left, matching its writing direction. Additionally, some symbols can draw from their center, like this symmetrical symbol.

sources.title: Build a SwiftUI app with the new design
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Make Liquid Glass adapt automatically to underlying content darkness, changing from light to dark on scroll.
claims.quote: As you scroll through content, the glass automatically adapts to the content underneath, changing from light to dark.

claims.rule: Use backgroundExtensionEffect to extend content outside safe area without clipping when behind overlays.
claims.quote: With the new backgroundExtensionEffect modifier, views can extend outside the safe area, without clipping their content.

claims.rule: Configure tab bar to minimize on scroll to prioritize content visibility over navigation chrome.
claims.quote: With the new design, the tab bar on iPhone floats above the content, and can be configured to minimize on scroll. This lets your app's content remain the star of the show.

claims.rule: Remove custom backgrounds from sheets to let the new Liquid Glass material display properly.
claims.quote: If you've used the presentationBackground modifier to apply a custom background to your sheets, consider removing that and let the new material shine.

claims.rule: Use glassEffectContainer to group multiple glass elements so they share a consistent sampling region.
claims.quote: Using a glass container allows these elements to share their sampling region, providing a consistent visual result.

claims.rule: Use concentric rectangle shapes to maintain corner alignment between views and their containers across different displays.
claims.quote: To build views that automatically maintain concentricity with their container, use the concentric rectangle shape. Pass the containerConcentric configuration to the corner parameter of a rectangle and the shape will automatically match its container across different displays and window shapes.

claims.rule: Use monochrome icon rendering in toolbars to reduce visual noise and emphasize app content.
claims.quote: Icons use monochrome rendering in more places, including in toolbars. The monochrome palette reduces visual noise, emphasizes your app's content, and maintains legibility.

sources.title: Create icons with Icon Composer
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use vector formats like SVG for icon design to ensure maximum scalability across different sizes and resolutions.
claims.quote: it's best to use a tool that can draw in vectors since having the ability to export SVGs will give you the most scalability

claims.rule: Structure icons with distinct layers representing depth to enable dynamic material effects like glass properties and lighting.
claims.quote: each layer represents a step in Z depth, where the bottom is the background and the other stack on top

claims.rule: Convert text to outlines before exporting SVG layers for icons, since SVG format does not preserve font information.
claims.quote: If I was to use any text too, since the SVG format doesn't preserve fonts, it will need converting to outlines before exporting.

claims.rule: Use four or fewer groups (containing up to four layers each) per icon to maintain visual complexity within optimal bounds.
claims.quote: We found this number provides the right bounds for how much visual complexity an icon should have.

claims.rule: Set at least one mono-mode icon element to white and map other colors to gray tones to maximize legibility in monochrome.
claims.quote: Setting at least one element of your icon to be white, usually the most prominent or recognizable part, make sure it shows up strong.

claims.rule: Keep source icon artwork flat, opaque, and simple; add dynamic effects like blur and shadow only in Icon Composer, not the source file.
claims.quote: it's best for me to still my source art down to its graphic essence, so that it's flat, opaque, and easy to control later.

sources.title: Better together: SwiftUI and RealityKit
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Make animation playback controllable and observable in SwiftUI to allow users to pause, resume, and scrub through 3D model animations.
claims.quote: The asset vends an `animationPlaybackController`. Use this object to pause, resume, and seek in the animation.

claims.rule: Make RealityKit AnimationPlaybackController observable in SwiftUI to allow real-time UI updates of animation playback state and scrubbing.
claims.quote: In visionOS 26, the existing RealityKit class `AnimationPlaybackController` is now Observable.

claims.rule: Use realityViewLayoutBehavior modifier with fixedSize to make RealityView tightly wrap 3D model bounds like Model3D does by default.
claims.quote: I apply the new `.realityViewLayoutBehavior` modifier with `.fixedSize` to make the RealityView tightly wrap the model's initial bounds.

claims.rule: Add both InputTargetComponent and CollisionComponent to gesture targets in RealityKit to ensure the interaction system recognizes entity gestures.
claims.quote: Pro tip: on any entity that's the target of a gesture, also add both InputTargetComponent and CollisionComponent.

sources.title: Say hello to the new look of app icons
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Layer visual elements by depth to create a sense of dimension and physical presence in app icons.
claims.quote: The material layers different elements like edge highlights, frostiness, and translucency to not only add a sense of depth

claims.rule: Use translucency and frostiness effects to make icons appear lit from within and enhance visual expressiveness.
claims.quote: it really makes it seem as if the icons are lit from within. And adding to this physicality, the material comes alive

claims.rule: Use unified grid-based design across platforms to maintain visual consistency while supporting multiple device formats.
claims.quote: we've now made it easier to design across our devices for both rounded rectangle and circle formats. Let's start with our rounded rectangle shape. We've updated the design grid to a simpler and more evenly spaced structure.

claims.rule: Use frontal, flat perspectives and avoid realistic 3D objects in icon designs, as they compete with material glass effects rather than complement them.
claims.quote: Realistic 3D objects and perspectives like in the previous Chess icon can compete with the material qualities. The redesigned icon uses a frontal view and a more flat appearance.

sources.title: What’s new in Xcode 26
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Enable search across multiple words and their proximity clusters to help users navigate large codebases effectively.
claims.quote: I can enter a set of words. For example, here, I'm trying to find where in my project I'm creating clipped resizable images. Xcode will now find all the clusters of these words in proximity to each other

claims.rule: Improve typing latency in complex code expressions to enhance developer experience and reduce friction.
claims.quote: optimized text input in Xcode this year, improving typing latency in some complex expressions by up to 50%

claims.rule: Load workspaces 40% faster by optimizing initialization and resource allocation for large projects.
claims.quote: It's now 40% faster to load a workspace. For large projects, this makes a big difference.

claims.rule: Enable voice control to write code by understanding Swift syntax, spacing, operators, and camel-casing from natural speech.
claims.quote: Voice Control understands Swift syntax. It will figure out where spaces should appear, whether expressions correspond to operators or should be camel-cased

claims.rule: Show code changes incrementally and let users undo them by preserving snapshots before each AI-generated modification.
claims.quote: Xcode keeps a snapshot of your code before each change is applied, so you can easily view and unwind them using the modification history

sources.title: Set the scene with SwiftUI in visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Avoid auto-restoring transient UI elements like welcome screens, context-dependent tools, or one-time actions when relaunching an app.
claims.quote: Consider disabling scene restoration for transient elements like a welcome screen, context-dependent UI like a tools window tied to a specific app state, or completed one-time actions like a login prompt.

claims.rule: Persist user-locked windows and volumes in their original rooms to create a sense of presence and continuity in spatial interfaces.
claims.quote: visionOS 26 brings over some macOS lifecycle APIs that will come in quite handy. We'll cover APIs to manage scene restoration and app launch as well as an API to create unique windows. In visionOS 26, people can now persist windows, volumes, and even the new widgets by locking them to particular rooms in their physical surroundings.

sources.title: Say hello to the next generation of CarPlay design system
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use variable typefaces with continuous scaling for weight, width, and corner softness to enable rich customization without limiting to preset styles.
claims.quote: Our variable fonts allow qualities like weight and width both extended and condensed as well as the softness of the corners to all exist on a continuous scale

claims.rule: Enable customization of gauge arc, start points, and end points to adapt to brand identity and hardware configurations.
claims.quote: Circular gauges let you decide the arc of the gauge too, as well as it's start and end points

sources.title: Elevate your tab and sidebar experience in iPadOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Position tab bars at the top of the app, closer to navigation controls, to make them easier to reach.
claims.quote: The bar now sits at the top of the app, where it is closer to other navigation controls, making it easier to reach.

claims.rule: Limit the number of tabs to avoid making it harder for people to locate information within your app.
claims.quote: Avoid adding too many tabs. Too many choices make it harder for people to locate information within your app.

claims.rule: Use outline glyph variants for tab symbols; the system automatically selects the filled variant in tab bars.
claims.quote: Tab bars prefer filled glyphs, and sidebars prefer outlined glyphs. When using symbol images for your tabs, use the outline variant. The system will automatically select the filled variant when displayed in the tab bar.

claims.rule: Keep tab state consistent between iPhone and iPad so people can navigate easily regardless of device.
claims.quote: Tabs should be consistent between iPhone and iPad to allow people to navigate easily no matter what device they are using.

claims.rule: Persist tab customizations automatically so users do not lose their organized layout.
claims.quote: Customizations to the order and visibility are automatically persisted.

claims.rule: Designate fixed tabs for essential app destinations to prevent users from hiding them.
claims.quote: The fixed section is designed for important destinations of your app. They appear before other items and disallow customization.

claims.rule: Place search functionality in the pinned trailing section of tab bars for consistent access.
claims.quote: Items in the pinned section, like search, are always available in the trailing edge of the tab bar.

sources.title: Explore multiview video playback in visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Enable multiview layout templates that maximize comfort and ergonomics when displaying multiple simultaneous video screens.
claims.quote: Multiview allows up to five video screens at once, with layout templates that maximize comfort and viewability.

claims.rule: Designate one video as main-focus to receive direct playback controls and audio priority in multiview experiences.
claims.quote: The original video has main focus, which includes a slightly more prominent look and audio playback. When I close the content browser, I get the familiar media playback controls and the main-focus video responds directly to these controls.

claims.rule: Start with single-view playback and suggest multiview only when users explicitly opt in.
claims.quote: Start out with the familiar single watch experience. For someone who wants to take it up a notch, suggest multiview using the standard button offered by AVPlayerViewController.

claims.rule: Use title and thumbnail previews in content browsers; minimize decorations to aid identification.
claims.quote: Describe each piece of content succinctly with a title and thumbnail preview of the content. The browser area is limited relative to the video screens, so minimize decorations and focus on elements that facilitate identification.

sources.title: Design great visionOS apps
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use photorealistic assets with high visual quality to make spatial content feel convincing and compelling.
claims.quote: As a baseline, assets need to be photorealistic with a high degree of visual quality to feel convincing and compelling.

claims.rule: Bring spatial content to life through animations that replicate real scenarios or enable manipulation not easily done in reality.
claims.quote: To make new things possible, bring your content to life. Consider how animations can replicate real scenarios, like you see here with air simulation in the intake fan. Or provide ways to manipulate models that would be cumbersome in the real world.

claims.rule: Keep app windows cohesive and contained; anchor controls outside but linked to the view.
claims.quote: The content and UI of your app should be contained in a window. Controls like Tab bars and Toolbars can live outside the window, but they are still anchored to the view.

claims.rule: Use Glass material for windows so they adapt intelligently to the user's environment lighting.
claims.quote: Visually comfortable experiences are those that feel part of the operating system which was designed to blend with the world. Like the Glass material used for windows. Since there isn't a concept of light and dark mode on visionOS, Glass is rendered through the system and intelligently adapts to the lighting in peoples environment.

claims.rule: Apply hover effects only to interactive elements; avoid them on read-only data to reduce confusion.
claims.quote: Every element that's interactive and has a detail view, like hourly temperatures, uses a hover effect. But the data that is meant to be read like details around dawn and dusk, don't require a hover effect.

claims.rule: Use at least 60 points of tap target space for interactive elements to prevent user frustration.
claims.quote: Keep in mind, interactive elements need sufficient tap targets, so use at least 60 points of space.

claims.rule: Use subtle animation like pulsing outlines to guide users toward the first required interaction.
claims.quote: Notice the pulsing stroke outline around the music icon. This is a subtle way to guide you to tap on the music library. It's a simple detail with a big impact.

claims.rule: Automate complex manual processes hidden from the user to reduce cognitive load and focus on creative tasks.
claims.quote: In the 3D environment, we asked ourselves, 'Why a DJ would even need to manually match tempos? When we could completely automate the process under the hood?' This abstraction not only reduces complexity, but also enhances the user's ability to focus more on the creative aspects of DJing.

sources.title: Enhance your UI animations and transitions
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Make zoom transitions continuously interactive, allowing users to grab and drag the element during the transition.
claims.quote: With this new transition, the cell you tap morphs into the incoming view. And it's not just a new visual appearance, it also is continuously interactive, allowing you to grab and drag it around, from the beginning or during the transition.

claims.rule: Use SwiftUI Animation types to animate UIKit views instead of computing initial velocity manually.
claims.quote: SwiftUI animations already have the ability to preserve velocity at the end of a gesture by merging together during the gesture

claims.rule: Reset transition state by viewDidAppear or viewDidDisappear, which are guaranteed to be called at transition end.
claims.quote: reset it by viewDidAppear or viewDidDisappear. These are guaranteed to be called at the end of the transition

sources.title: Design advanced games for Apple platforms
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Bundle the first 15 minutes of gameplay into the initial app download to let players start immediately upon installation.
claims.quote: Aim to get around the first 15 minutes of gameplay bundled into your App Store download.

claims.rule: Hide background downloads from players; load additional game data behind the scenes after installation.
claims.quote: Try to hide download progress from players. In many cases they'll never have to know that data is still loading in, and it will feel like your whole game was playable at launch.

claims.rule: Set sensible defaults automatically based on device hardware to reduce onboarding choices for players.
claims.quote: You can simplify your game's onboarding by setting options automatically for players. For example, in your onboarding and settings, look for places to remove choices that aren't relevant. Like asking for screen size or aspect ratio, which you just get from the device itself.

claims.rule: Automatically detect paired controllers and map buttons to UI without requiring manual player setup.
claims.quote: Instead of having folks manually set up a physical game controller, you can automatically detect whether a controller is paired and get its profile by using the Game Controller Framework.

claims.rule: Adjust initial performance settings to match device capabilities across different platforms.
claims.quote: When choosing defaults across different platforms, consider adjusting your game's initial performance settings to match the capabilities of that device. For example, you might choose to set quality defaults higher, for a top-of-the-line Mac, than you would for an iPhone.

claims.rule: Reduce settings granularity on mobile platforms to prioritize quick startup and simplified choices.
claims.quote: Especially on mobile platforms, remember that players just want to pick up their device and go. So look for opportunities where you can reduce the granularity of your settings, compared to what you might offer on a desktop.

claims.rule: Anchor game UI sections to specific screen sides rather than scaling uniformly to fit different aspect ratios.
claims.quote: break your UI layout into separate sections. Each of which is anchored to a specific side of the screen. As you move between device shapes, you can keep each section at a consistent size

sources.title: Design Live Activities for Apple Watch
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Make Live Activities on Apple Watch highly glanceable, showing only the most critical information needed.
claims.quote: Live Activities on Apple Watch are meant to be highly glanceable, providing just the information you need, and nothing more.

claims.rule: Display a compact Live Activity view at the bottom of the screen when updates occur while users are in another app.
claims.quote: To ensure people never miss an update from your Live Activity we've created the compact view When you're interacting with an app and a Live Activity receives an update, like the status of your food delivery changing, a smaller, more compact version of the Live Activity appears at the bottom of the display.

claims.rule: Auto-present the Smart Stack when a Live Activity starts so users can see status by raising their wrist.
claims.quote: On Apple Watch, when a Live Activity starts, the Smart Stack is automatically presented and displays a widget for that Live Activity. This allows you to see the status of a Live Activity just by raising your wrist, without having to first rotate the Digital Crown.

sources.title: Explore game input in visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Let players make small hand movements that amplify into big actions; use indirect input for comfortable longer play sessions.
claims.quote: Indirect input lets players make small hand movements that are amplified into big actions.

claims.rule: For direct input interactions, include abundant visual and audio feedback so every contact feels satisfying.
claims.quote: If this type of input fits your game, make sure to include plenty of feedback, so every contact with an object feels satisfying for the player.

claims.rule: Prefer system gestures; players already know them and need no extra equipment or learning.
claims.quote: For one thing, players already know exactly how to use the system gestures, because they're already using them to navigate all the other apps and games on the platform.

claims.rule: For direct-input games, combine visual and audio feedback so every contact feels satisfying; use effects like lightning streaks and impact sounds.
claims.quote: make sure to include plenty of feedback, so every contact with an object feels satisfying for the player. You can use a combination of visual feedback, like the lightning streak behind your hand and the flying pulp. And you can add sounds, like squishing and splashing.

claims.rule: Prefer system gestures over custom ones; players already know them, need no extra equipment, and they work across all spaces without learning overhead.
claims.quote: players already know exactly how to use the system gestures, because they're already using them to navigate all the other apps and games on the platform. You won't need to teach them how to interact with your game. And there's no extra equipment needed.

claims.rule: If using custom gestures, keep them sparse, simple, and intuitive; teach them during onboarding with visual and audio feedback so players learn and remember them.
claims.quote: Any custom gestures you create for your game need to be easy for players to learn, and easy for them to remember. Make sure the gestures are a great fit for the action in your game so they'll be intuitive.

claims.rule: Auto-detect connected game controllers and switch input handling; do not require players to find a settings menu to enable controller support.
claims.quote: Detecting that a controller is connected, and switching your input over to work with that controller, is much better than making the player search for a switch in your game's Settings menu.

claims.rule: Ensure all game UI and actions are accessible via game controller when one is connected; do not require system gestures for any part of the experience.
claims.quote: make sure you can do everything in the game with the controller. Expecting players to use a system gesture to access part of your UI would be inconvenient and pretty confusing.

sources.title: What’s new in SF Symbols 6
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use Wiggle animation to highlight changes or call-to-action elements that might be overlooked.
claims.quote: You can use the Wiggle preset when you want to highlight changes or a call to action that might be overlooked.

claims.rule: Use Breathe animation to convey status changes or signal that an activity is taking place with more lifelike presence.
claims.quote: Breathe is the animation that smoothly increases and decreases the presence of a symbol, giving it a living quality.

claims.rule: Use Rotate animation to indicate progress or imitate real-world object behavior as a visual indicator.
claims.quote: With Rotate you can add dynamic movement to a symbol by imitating how an object behaves in the real world, or by acting as a visual indicator.

claims.rule: Use Breathe animation to convey status changes or ongoing activity; Breathe modulates opacity and size for lifelike presence, unlike Pulse which uses opacity alone.
claims.quote: Breathe is the animation that smoothly increases and decreases the presence of a symbol, giving it a living quality. It helps convey status changes, or it can signal that an activity is taking place.

claims.rule: Use animations intentionally and sparingly; too many or misplaced animations overwhelm and distract from content and critical actions.
claims.quote: Animations are great in UI, but using too many or in the wrong context can make it feel overwhelming and distracting, drawing attention away from important content and actions.

sources.title: Create custom environments for your immersive apps in visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Simplify 3D geometry to only the complexity necessary to communicate assets with enough detail; decimate distant assets.
claims.quote: Geometry should be as complex as necessary to communicate the asset with enough detail.

claims.rule: Use texture baking to combine all surface characteristics into single images, reducing total textures and computational load.
claims.quote: Texture Baking, which captures all surface characteristics of 3D objects into a single image. This image can then be reapplied to the objects, making them look realistic and detailed without additional raytracing.

claims.rule: Test lighting perception on both monitor and headset, as they differ; offer multiple lighting modes for viewer choice.
claims.quote: As you test the lighting, it is important to note that how you perceive light varies between monitor and headset.

claims.rule: Simplify geometry to necessary complexity; decimate distant assets to reduce computational load while maintaining perceived detail.
claims.quote: Geometry should be as complex as necessary to communicate the asset with enough detail. As the tree asset is located at the back of the scene, and it requires less detail, so in this case, the tree asset can be decimated.

sources.title: Design interactive experiences for visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Design for variable environments; what works indoors in a living room may not work outdoors in a park.
claims.quote: What works indoors in someone's living room might not work outdoors in a park.

claims.rule: Test interactive experiences in device frequently; prototype often to validate assumptions before shipping.
claims.quote: everything changes once you're testing in device. You may imagine how things are going to look and feel while designing, but you can't know for certain until you test them. Prototype and test your ideas in device as often as you can.

claims.rule: Use proximity, motion, and sound to implicitly cue interaction; lead users to objects they naturally want to touch.
claims.quote: use cues like proximity, motion, and sound to pull them in. And just make sure that your first interaction is with something small, simple, and welcoming to ease your audience in.

sources.title: Design App Intents for system experiences
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Surface all app functionality as app intents, not just habitual tasks; balance flexibility with clarity to avoid brittle intents.
claims.quote: Now, anything your app does should be an app intent.

claims.rule: Do not create app intents that exclusively trigger specific UI elements; intents should represent underlying tasks.
claims.quote: App intents should not exclusively trigger specific UI elements, such as tapping a cancel button, or swiping down on a platter.

claims.rule: Ensure parameter summaries remain readable as sentences regardless of which option is selected.
claims.quote: Since the parameter can be changed to any of these camera modes, it's important to make sure the summary is always readable as a sentence, regardless of which mode you select.

claims.rule: Open your app as part of intent completion to show the user that a change has occurred in the app state.
claims.quote: In iOS 18, opening your app is now a common behavior to show people that the intent has made a change in the app. Returning an open as part of your app intent gives people the option to see the change.

sources.title: Create custom hover effects in visionOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use hover effects to provide feedback about which element will trigger when users tap their fingers together.
claims.quote: Hover effects make your app feel responsive while providing feedback about which element will be triggered when people tap their fingers together.

claims.rule: Respect accessibility preferences when building custom hover effects; ensure effects are comfortable and preserve privacy.
claims.quote: Custom hover effects were designed from the ground up to preserve privacy. They're applied by the system, outside the app process.

claims.rule: Group hover effects to activate together when looking at any part of the group; use explicit or implicit grouping to control activation areas.
claims.quote: Grouped effects are applied together, whenever any effect in the group becomes active. When effects from different views are grouped together, the group becomes active when I look at any of those views.

sources.title: Add personality to your app through UX writing
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Define your app's voice through consistent qualities like clarity, simplicity, friendliness, and helpfulness that guide all writing.
claims.quote: Clarity, simplicity, friendliness, and helpfulness. Your voice will be different, but I see these pretty consistently throughout Apple's writing

claims.rule: Use exclamation points sparingly, reserving them for genuinely celebratory or urgent moments to maintain impact.
claims.quote: we tend to use exclamation marks pretty sparingly around here, this screen gets one, because of the situation

claims.rule: Modulate four core voice qualities—clarity, simplicity, friendliness, helpfulness—by turning each up or down based on the situation to adjust tone.
claims.quote: to help you dial in your tone for a specific situation, it can be helpful to think of each of these qualities as something that can be turned up or down

claims.rule: Read UX writing aloud to confirm it sounds like your app's intended personality before shipping.
claims.quote: Read your writing out loud. Ask yourself. Does this sound like the best version of your app?

claims.rule: Write inclusively to avoid jargon that excludes people unfamiliar with specialized terminology.
claims.quote: Avoid jargon. Not everyone knows it, so it can make people feel left out. On a related note, write inclusively.

sources.title: Create custom visual effects with SwiftUI
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Test visual effects over time and in different contexts to confirm they remain pleasant after novelty wears off.
claims.quote: Visual effects should be pleasant to use well after the novelty has worn off. Testing your effects over time, and in different contexts will help reinforce if an effect is working

claims.rule: Use scroll transitions to change rotation, offset, or opacity based on element position, creating unique scroll experiences.
claims.quote: Scroll transition exposes the content I'd like to transition, as well as a phase. I can use these values to change the rotation, and offset of each photo

claims.rule: Use scroll transitions to rotate, offset, or change opacity of list elements based on their scroll position to create unique, engaging scroll experiences.
claims.quote: Scroll transition exposes the content I'd like to transition, as well as a phase. I can use these values to change the rotation, and offset of each photo in my scroll view. Based on its position.

sources.title: Design and build apps for watchOS 10
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Anchor primary interactions to the Digital Crown, with touch as a backup, to match the watch's input paradigm.
claims.quote: In watchOS 10, we are emphasizing the Digital Crown as the way you get to and navigate through apps, to scroll, paginate, and make precise adjustments. While interactions should be anchored to the crown, they should also always be backed up by touch.

claims.rule: Land people directly in the detail view at app launch by intelligently surfacing the most relevant item based on location, recency, frequency, or user intent.
claims.quote: Land people directly in the detail view when they launch your app. Use location, recency, frequency, or some other indication of user intent to inform which detail to surface first.

claims.rule: Design watchOS detail views to be unmistakable at a glance so they require no title for clarity.
claims.quote: Strive to make your detail view so unmistakable at a glance that it doesn't need a title.

claims.rule: Use full-screen color and imagery in watchOS dial-based views to add context and reduce text dependency for dense information delivery.
claims.quote: Dial-based views are great for dense information delivered at a glance. The use of full screen color and imagery, like weather conditions, can help to add additional context.

sources.title: Q&A: watchOS 10 design
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

sources.title: Meet the presenters: Design with SwiftUI
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

sources.title: Design with SwiftUI
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Test interactions on the actual device to accurately validate how layouts, animations, and gestures feel in real use.
claims.quote: we developed all our designs in SwiftUI, right on device. This gave us control over every detail, from spacing and typestyles to animations and interactions.

claims.rule: Build designs on the actual device to surface interaction details and complexity hidden in static tools.
claims.quote: All of these details were initially opaque when we began designing. But the moment we started making prototypes, they were obvious.

claims.rule: Use on-device demos to communicate designs more effectively than slides; demos explain themselves and build consensus.
claims.quote: When people can hold a demo of your work in their hands, designs explain themselves. This helps build consensus and can save everyone the hassle of more meetings.

sources.title: Design for spatial input
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Place main content in the center of the field of view; reserve edges for secondary actions only.
claims.quote: Try to keep the main content of the app in the center of the field of view, the most comfortable area for your eyes.

claims.rule: Keep all interactive content at the same depth to avoid eye strain from refocusing.
claims.quote: Look to keep interactive content at the same depth to make it feel effortless to switch between UI.

claims.rule: Use round shapes and avoid sharp edges to guide eye focus to element centers.
claims.quote: Use round shapes like circles, pills, and rounded rectangles. Avoid using shapes with sharp edges.

claims.rule: Use round shapes and avoid sharp edges to guide eye focus to element centers and improve targeting accuracy.
claims.quote: To help our eyes, use round shapes like circles, pills, and rounded rectangles. Avoid using shapes with sharp edges.

claims.rule: Maintain a minimum target area of 60 points by combining size and spacing for eye-based interaction.
claims.quote: The minimum area that your element needs for eye target is 60 points. But the element can be smaller than 60 points. You can achieve the minimum target area combining size and spacing.

claims.rule: Use dynamic scaling so UI maintains the same field-of-view coverage and target area size regardless of window distance.
claims.quote: Dynamic scale keeps your UI and the target areas at the same size, while fixed scale changes the size and makes the target areas too small.

sources.title: Make features discoverable with TipKit
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Target tips only to users who would benefit; use eligibility rules to avoid reaching uninterested or already-informed audiences.
claims.quote: In-app education should be focused on those who would benefit from it, and we aim to avoid getting in the way of individuals while they are trying to accomplish something in an app.

claims.rule: Control tip frequency so multiple tips do not appear simultaneously; stagger them across hours or days to avoid overwhelming users.
claims.quote: The tips are all useful but would be less effective if they all showed up at once. With TipKit, I can set the display frequency for the tips, so they appear at a more ideal cadence.

claims.rule: Dismiss tips once users perform the described action or reach maximum display count to remove outdated education.
claims.quote: Once they see the tip and tap the favorite button, I'll call the invalidate method with the reason `.userPerformedAction` to signify that the desired outcome has been performed and the tip will be dismissed.

sources.title: Design widgets for the Smart Stack on Apple Watch
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Show only essential information on Watch widgets; people spend about ten seconds max engaging with glanceable content.
claims.quote: people should only be spending around ten seconds max engaging with glanceable information on their Watch

claims.rule: Use standard design layouts for Watch widgets to ensure visual consistency and smooth reading experience.
claims.quote: visual consistency is key to providing a smooth and predictable reading experience

claims.rule: Make widgets recognizable and distinctive by choosing background colors that convey meaning or assist app recognition.
claims.quote: choose a color for their widget background that assists in app recognition or conveys informational meaning

claims.rule: Prioritize widgets to appear in Smart Stack based on imminent time/date, reached location, detected headphones, sleep/wake times, or workout activity.
claims.quote: when a time and date is imminent, when a location has been reached, when headphones are detected, when a person wakes up or when they're going to bed, or when a person starts or ends a Workout

sources.title: Q&A: UX writing
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

sources.title: Design Shortcuts for Spotlight
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Design shortcuts to perform direct actions, not mirror tab-bar navigation or secondary workflows.
claims.quote: Prefer shortcuts that take action directly. Your first idea might be to look at your app's tab bar and reflect it directly into shortcuts, but challenge yourself to think of something better.

claims.rule: Order shortcuts to match the user's mental model and decisions made inside the app to build muscle memory.
claims.quote: You should order your shortcuts to reflect the decisions people make inside your app, and to help people build muscle memory around things being in predictable places.

claims.rule: Focus app shortcuts on essential, habitual actions and content; do not fill all spaces with shortcuts.
claims.quote: focus on the essential, habitual actions and content from your app

claims.rule: Order shortcuts to match user's mental model and reflect decisions made inside the app to build muscle memory.
claims.quote: order your shortcuts to reflect the decisions people make inside your app, and to help people build muscle memory

claims.rule: Make shortcut titles concise and avoid truncation; never include app name since it is shown separately.
claims.quote: keeping your titles concise to avoid truncation and never include your app name

sources.title: Animate symbols in your app
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Use discrete symbol effects for one-off animations triggered by user events; use indefinite effects for continuous animations.
claims.quote: Bounce, for example, plays a one-off animation on the symbol. This is considered discrete behavior. Adding a Scale effect, on the other hand, changes the symbol's scale level and keeps it there indefinitely

claims.rule: Apply symbol animations to multiple related symbols by adding the effect on a parent view; use symbolEffectsRemoved to prevent inheritance when needed.
claims.quote: the symbolEffect modifier propagates through the view hierarchy. This means effects can be applied to multiple images by adding the modifier on a parent view

sources.title: Design dynamic Live Activities
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Prioritize information visibility by sizing and scaling elements to be visible at a quick glance.
claims.quote: Think about the information you would find most useful and prioritize the sizing and scale of those elements to be visible at a quick glance.

claims.rule: Maintain visual connection between Live Activity and app by sharing colors, iconography, and typeface.
claims.quote: As you design your graphical layout, consider the colors, iconography, typefaces, and other attributes from your app that you can use. The goal and best end result is when your Live Activity and app feel like they share the same visual aesthetic and personality.

claims.rule: Preserve color associations between Light and Dark modes to maintain visual connection with app icon.
claims.quote: Don't alter your colors between light and dark mode if it breaks this visual association.

claims.rule: Integrate logo marks into layout structure rather than displaying the full app icon.
claims.quote: If you do use a logo mark as part of your brand, make sure it's integrated uncontained into the layout itself rather than just using your whole app icon.

claims.rule: Dynamically adjust Live Activity height based on available information to reduce clutter.
claims.quote: Another way to use space efficiently is to dynamically change the height of your Live Activity between different moments as you have more or less information to display.

claims.rule: Reduce Live Activity height dynamically when information decreases to minimize lock screen space.
claims.quote: dynamically change the height of your Live Activity between different moments as you have more or less information to display

claims.rule: Use numeric content transition to animate counting numbers and content-replace transition for graphic elements.
claims.quote: Use the numeric content transition to count up or down important numbers in your Activity. And for animating in and out graphic elements and text, use the content replace transition.

claims.rule: Remove Live Activities from lock screen after a short duration when they end to avoid manual dismissal.
claims.quote: make sure to remove it from the lock screen after a short duration of time, as it can be annoying if it sticks around too long

claims.rule: Keep Dynamic Island content concentric by using even margins and nesting rounded shapes inside each other.
claims.quote: A key aspect to making things fit nicely inside the Dynamic Island is for them to be concentric with its shape. This is when rounded shapes nest inside of each other with even margins all the way around.

claims.rule: Make Dynamic Island Compact view as narrow as possible with content snug against the sensor region.
claims.quote: A key goal is for the encapsulation to be as narrow as possible with no wasted space. Ensure content is snug against the sensor region.

claims.rule: Maintain relative placement of elements between Dynamic Island Compact and Expanded views for coherence.
claims.quote: When laying out your expanded view, try and maintain the relative placement of things between the two views. That way there's a coherence between them.

sources.title: Q&A: Widgets in the Smart Stack on watchOS
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

sources.title: Design considerations for vision and motion
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Ensure all depth cues in 3D content align to give the brain correct depth information.
claims.quote: Ensure all of the depth cues from your content give the brain correct information so to align the viewer's eyes to the depth you intended.

claims.rule: Add missing depth cues using color, blur, relative size, motion, background, light, shadow, occlusion, and texture.
claims.quote: An added background, light and shadow, occlusion, and texture density are some more methods to add in the missing visual depth cues.

claims.rule: Place content requiring extended fixation farther than arm's-length distance for visual comfort.
claims.quote: Content requiring fixating the eyes for an extended time, such as for reading, is most visually comfortable when placed farther than arm's-length distance.

claims.rule: Enable users to adjust content depth to choose a comfortable distance for their viewing.
claims.quote: In addition, enable a person to adjust content depth so they may choose a depth that's most comfortable for them in the experience.

claims.rule: Place content requiring extended reading farther than arm's length and allow depth adjustment for viewer comfort.
claims.quote: Content requiring fixating the eyes for an extended time, such as for reading, is most visually comfortable when placed farther than arm's-length distance. In addition, enable a person to adjust content depth

claims.rule: Make moving objects semitransparent so passthrough is visible and brain interprets motion correctly.
claims.quote: you can mitigate this by making objects semitransparent when they move, so the passthrough content is clearly visible during the motion

claims.rule: Keep camera focus of expansion slow, predictable and within field of view to prevent motion discomfort.
claims.quote: you want to move the camera in such a way that the motion of the focus of expansion is slow and predictable, and you want to keep the focus of expansion within the field of view

claims.rule: Avoid oscillations at 0.2 Hz frequency; if unavoidable keep amplitude low and content semitransparent.
claims.quote: try to avoid oscillations in general, and in particular those with frequencies around 0.2 Hz. That is one oscillation per 5 seconds. And if you really cannot avoid showing oscillating motions, try to keep the amplitude of the motion low

sources.title: Design spatial SharePlay experiences
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Present windowed shared activities to support multitasking and collaboration without leaving surroundings.
claims.quote: Putting your activity in a window is a great way to support multitasking and collaboration and doesn't require people to leave their surroundings.

claims.rule: Minimize setup steps when joining shared activities; start activity for permitted users and show placeholders for others.
claims.quote: Minimize the amount of setup involved in joining. If your shared activity does need additional steps to get started, start the activity for people who have the right permissions and present a placeholder window to those who don't.

claims.rule: Avoid launching extra windows unrelated to the shared activity.
claims.quote: When possible, don't launch any extra windows unrelated to the shared activity.

claims.rule: Synchronize state changes and animations across all participants to make gestures and interactions meaningful.
claims.quote: Your app needs to synchronize everyone's view of content, showing animations and any state changes in lockstep. This is key to making gestures like pointing make sense to everyone on the call.

claims.rule: Allow personalized controls for accessibility while keeping main shared context identical across participants.
claims.quote: While it's important to share as much context across devices as possible, look for opportunities for software to improve on the physical limitations of real-world social experiences, especially when it comes to comfort and accessibility.

claims.rule: Allow individuals to open separate personal windows while maintaining shared context for group coordination.
claims.quote: If individuals want to separately dive in on another part of the document, you could always allow each person to open a personal window, as if they brought their own iPad to the meeting.

sources.title: Q&A: Spatial design
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

sources.title: Design for spatial user interfaces
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Keep app icon graphics centered to avoid appearing off-center when expanded.
claims.quote: Try to keep graphics centered. If they are too close to the edge, they could look off-center when expanded.

claims.rule: Avoid large semitransparent regions in app icon layers to prevent blending with shadows.
claims.quote: Avoid using large regions of semitransparent pixels. Layers with reduced opacity will blend with the shadow cast behind it.

claims.rule: Avoid stacking multiple lighter materials to maintain legibility and contrast.
claims.quote: Try to not stack lighter materials on top of each other, as it impacts legibility and reduces contrast.

claims.rule: Keep interactive elements centered with at least 60 points of tap target area, adding 8 points minimum spacing around smaller visual elements.
claims.quote: Interactive elements must have a tap target area with at least 60 points of space, so they can be easily selected. This means that your UI element can be visually smaller, like the standard button, which is 44 points, as long as you add enough space around it.

claims.rule: Limit tab bar to six items maximum to keep the interface light and navigable.
claims.quote: In general, you want to keep those feeling light, so avoid having more than six items.

claims.rule: Use white text or symbols over glass material colors when color options make text visibility difficult.
claims.quote: Colorful elements on top of the glass may be hard to see if the color of the glass is similar. Most of the time, consider using white text or symbols so they are always clearly visible.

claims.rule: Place ornaments overlapping the bottom edge by 20 points to integrate them visually with the main window.
claims.quote: When ornaments sit at the bottom edge of the window, place them so they overlap the bottom edge by 20 points. This helps ornaments to feel like they're integrated with the main window without blocking too much content.

claims.rule: Keep UI in people's field of view; avoid placing content too high, too low, or too far down due to head rotation limits.
claims.quote: Because of the neck's range of motion, it's easier for most people to turn their head farther to the right and to the left rather than up and down. So keep your UI in people's field of view and be careful about placing anything too high up or too far down.

claims.rule: Use wider aspect ratios with horizontal canvas extension rather than vertical to accommodate ergonomic head movement.
claims.quote: If you need a large canvas for your app, go with a wider aspect ratio than taller. For example, in Freeform, the canvas extends horizontally and not vertically.

sources.title: Explore immersive sound design
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Vary pitch and amplitude of repetitive interaction sounds to feel more natural than static repetition.
claims.quote: when you know a sound will be played often, it helps to slightly randomize some elements of the sound like its pitch and amplitude

claims.rule: Use spatial audio to place interaction sounds at their visual locations on screen for natural feedback.
claims.quote: the sound of each key press and how it comes from its location on the keyboard in front of you. Each time you interact with the keys, the familiar sound confirms your action

claims.rule: Randomize pitch and amplitude of repetitive sounds to feel natural rather than static over time.
claims.quote: When you know a sound will be played often, it helps to slightly randomize some elements of the sound like its pitch and amplitude. It feels more natural and less static when keys are pressed in rapid succession.

claims.rule: Use distance and volume together to position sounds naturally; reduce volume and push location back to avoid harsh proximity.
claims.quote: It's way too loud and feels too close, so we need to do two things. First, turn down the volume of each a few decibels, And then push the location of the sound into the distance so it can sound further away.

sources.title: What’s new in SF Symbols 5
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Animate symbols by layer separately to create clear, precise choreography that guides visual hierarchy.
claims.quote: By default, a symbol will animate by layer. This means that each layer will animate one at a time, making the symbol's choreography have clear and precise movements

claims.rule: Animate symbols layer by layer by default to create clear, precise choreography that guides visual hierarchy.
claims.quote: By default, a symbol will animate by layer. This means that each layer will animate one at a time, making the symbol's choreography have clear and precise movements.

claims.rule: Use Bounce animation to confirm actions or indicate state changes; use Scale to provide focus or selection feedback.
claims.quote: Bounce communicates that an action has occurred or that an action needs to take place. Scale, on the other hand, can provide focus or feedback when an item is selected. In addition to that, this effect is also stateful, meaning the scaled state persists until the effect is removed.

claims.rule: Balance expressive animations with functional clarity; avoid overwhelming interfaces and prioritize the intended goal.
claims.quote: All these new presets can serve as a communication tool between a person and the interface and have a crucial role in enhancing the user experience, but it's important to work on achieving the right balance between attention-grabbing animations and a functional interface, so that the experience doesn't result in something overwhelming.

sources.title: Create animated symbols
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Annotate custom symbols to specify which layers should animate when using layer-by-layer animation presets.
claims.quote: a new control in the annotation list here that allows you to specify which layers should pulse when you're using the By Layer setting

sources.title: Meet watchOS 10
sources.why: Apple design-team session from the WWDC design track.

claims.rule: Make background content supporting, not decorative; it should provide utility aligned with the app's function.
claims.quote: Background content in watchOS 10 should play a supporting role that provides additional utility, not merely be a visual flourish

claims.rule: Use translucent materials to establish hierarchy and help users understand navigation context within the system.
claims.quote: Distinct, functional layers utilize translucency to establish hierarchy and help users understand where they are in the system or inside an app

claims.rule: Limit each watchOS page to single screen height to encourage focused purpose and glanceability.
claims.quote: we advise limiting the content of an individual page to a single screen height. Embracing this constraint encourages each page to serve a clear and distinct purpose and results in a more glanceable design.

claims.rule: Use vertical pagination instead of horizontal pagination for watchOS navigation.
claims.quote: Use Vertical Pagination in place of horizontal pagination, which is more difficult to navigate on Apple Watch.

claims.rule: Smoothly animate elements between pages using scale and position changes to maintain object permanence.
claims.quote: Smoothly animate elements between pages by manipulating their scale, position, and information density, instead of introducing additional instances of that element on each page. This object permanence helps provide a visual anchor for users as they navigate through full-screen pages of content.

claims.rule: Use background colors and content to aid navigation and app recognition, not as mere visual flourish.
claims.quote: Background content in watchOS 10 should play a supporting role that provides additional utility, not merely be a visual flourish.
